To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the microbiome, metabolome, and fermentation behavior of wine grape fermentations vary with the grape source, and that the microbiome of the grape and the metabolome of the wine can predict fermentation behavior.
the microbial communities of wine grapes and wines are highly variable, but the variation is structured by the vineyard site and the grape cultivar.

the microbial communities of wine grape must and wine are highly variable and that the composition of microbial communities is associated with wine metabolome, fermentation behavior, and regional origin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the detection of the wine spoilage yeast, Brettanomyces/Dekkera bruxellensis, using a combination of PCR, real-time PCR and a novel DNA microarray.
the characterization and quantification of the microbial communities associated with wine fermentation and the identification of their impact on wine quality.
the development of new methods and tools for monitoring and control of wine production, and with the understanding of the role of microorganisms in wine production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microbial community in the wine grape must and fermenting wine is a complex ecosystem that is affected by the vineyard, the winery, and the fermentation process.
the microbiota of grapes and wine is a complex ecosystem that is not fully understood.
the wine microbiota is not only a reflection of winemaking practices, but also a reflection of the grapes used in wine production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the microbiome and metabolome of wine grape berries, as well as the fermentation behavior of the berries, are associated with wine grape cultivar, and that there is a significant association between the microbiome and the metabolome of the wine grape berries.
we have identified a set of microbial communities that are associated with the wine making process and the production of regional wine characteristics.
the wine microbiome is highly dynamic and complex, but the microbiota is not a major contributor to the regional differences in wine flavor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microbiota and metabolome of wine grapes are associated with the microbiome and metabolome of finished wine, and the microbiome and fermentative behavior of the yeast starter.
the microbial community composition and activity of a wine ferment can have a significant impact on the final wine product, including its aroma and flavor profile.
the microbial communities associated with grapes and wines from different regions are different.
